raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not want to make big changes. Primary school is all I had, so I mostly farm by what I have seen over the years and what the good farmers nearby are doing. On my 15.3 mu, I will still keep the land split the familiar way: most of it in wheat-maize rotation, and the rest in cotton. Wheat and maize keep grain and cash coming, and cotton gives another way to earn if grain price is not good. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I cannot irrigate too freely. Some people in my house work off-farm, so labor at the busy times is tight. Because of that, I will keep the wheat-maize on about 10 mu and cotton on 5.3 mu. I will not chase very high input this year. If I put too little fertilizer, yield drops and that hurts more than spending a bit extra, but I also cannot empty my pocket all at once. So I will use moderate fertilizer, split it where it matters, irrigate the wheat a few key times, rush maize in right after wheat harvest, and manage cotton a bit more carefully because it needs more watching.
